title: Sprint Back: Protect the Paint
description: Defenders sprint back after a turnover, get below the ball, and stop the fast break with a hard early stance, building the first habit of transition defense.

content.objective: Get back below the ball at full speed, protect the basket first, then find a player and stop the attack.
content.setup: Three attackers start at the half-court line with the ball. Two defenders start one step behind them on the same line, as if they had just lost the ball. A third defender waits under the basket.
content.organization: Rotate groups every possession: attackers become defenders, defenders go to the back of the line.
instructions: On the coach's whistle the attackers push toward the basket, ball handler in the middle.
The two trailing defenders sprint to the paint first, turning their heads to see the ball as they run.
The defender under the basket calls the ball and points to where each teammate should go.
Defenders stop the ball as it crosses the free-throw line and stay between the attackers and the basket.
Play the possession to a score, a stop or a defensive rebound; the coach counts stops.
coachingPoints: Run to the paint, then to the ball: protect the basket first.
Communicate: call ball, call wing, call trailing runner.
Sprint with the chest turned so the ball and your player stay in view.
Do not chase the ball handler from behind; take an angle.
commonMistakes: Chasing the ball from behind and ending up out of position.
Both defenders stopping at the free-throw line instead of protecting the rim.
Silent defence: nobody calls the ball.
content.safety: Keep heads up while sprinting back and call "screen" if a teammate is in the way.
progressions: Start with a live rebound instead of a whistle so the defenders must read the shot.
regressions: Give the defenders a two-step head start until the habit is clear.
variations: Defenders earn one point for every stop before the free-throw line.
